Surely he came in with you, Toto?" "He did," said Toto, "but he hopped off the moment we entered. Didn't like the looks of the visitor, I fancy," he added in a low tone. Search was made, and finally the crow was discovered huddled together, a disconsolate little bunch of black feathers, in the darkest corner of the cave. "Come, Jim!" cried Toto, who was the first to catch sight of him. "Come out, old fellow! Why are you rumpling and humping yourself up in that absurd fashion?" "Is he gone?" asked the crow, opening one eye a very little way, and lifting his head a fraction of an inch from the mass of feathers in which it was buried. "Good Toto, kind Toto, is he gone? Preserve direction, negation and uncertainty in predicate wording. Return one JSON object only with keys entities and relations. entities is a list of {id, name, type, evidence}. relations is a list of {source, predicate, target, evidence}; source and target must refer to entity ids. Each evidence must be a verbatim substring of the passage that supports the item. Every entity MUST include an evidence field, even if the evidence is just its exact name as written in the passage. Every relation MUST include an evidence field. Before returning, verify all entities have all four required keys: id, name, type, evidence. Omit unsupported items. Use empty lists when appropriate. Return compact JSON without indentation. Do not repeat entities or relations. Do not create generic category nodes such as hotel or person merely to express an entity type. A relation must connect two independently identified entities and its evidence must support that specific pair.
